prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We introduce a family of rings of symmetric functions depending on an infinite sequence of parameters. A distinguished basis of such a ring is comprised by analogues of the Schur functions. The corresponding structure coefficients are polynomials in the parameters which we call the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials. We give a combinatorial rule for their calculation by modifying an earlier result of B. Sagan and the author. The new rule provides a formula for these polynomials which is manifestly positive in the sense of W. Graham. We apply this formula for the calculation of the product of equivariant Schubert classes on Grassmannians which implies a stability property of the structure coefficients. The first manifestly positive formula for such an expansion was given by A. Knutson and T. Tao by using combinatorics of puzzles while the stability property was not apparent from that formula. We also use the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials to describe the multiplication rule in the algebra of the Casimir elements for the general linear Lie algebra in the basis of the quantum immanants constructed by A. Okounkov and G. Olshanski.

We apply this formula to the calculation of products of equivariant Schubert classes on Grassmannians, which implies a stability property of the structure coefficients. The first manifestly positive formula for such an expansion was given by A. Knutson and T. Tao using the combinatorics of puzzles, although the stability property was not apparent from their formula.

We also use the Littlewood–Richardson polynomials to describe the multiplication rule in the algebra of Casimir elements for the general linear Lie algebra, with respect to the basis of quantum immanants constructed by A. Okounkov and G. Olshanski.

We define a class of symmetric-function rings governed by an infinite list of parameters. Within each ring there is a special basis consisting of functions that play the role of Schur functions. The multiplication constants for this basis are parameter-dependent polynomials, which we refer to as Littlewood–Richardson polynomials.

To compute these polynomials, we present a combinatorial rule obtained by adapting an earlier theorem of B. Sagan and the author. This revised rule yields a formula that is explicitly positive in W. Graham’s sense. We then use the formula to determine products of equivariant Schubert classes on Grassmannians, leading to a stability result for the associated structure constants. A. Knutson and T. Tao had previously produced the first explicitly positive expansion formula of this kind through puzzle combinatorics, though that approach did not make the stability phenomenon visible.

Finally, we employ the Littlewood–Richardson polynomials to express the multiplication law in the algebra of Casimir elements for the general linear Lie algebra, using the basis of quantum immanants introduced by A. Okounkov and G. Olshanski.

The text presents a family of rings of symmetric functions that depend on an infinite sequence of parameters. These rings generalize the classical ring of symmetric functions and provide a framework in which many familiar objects from algebraic combinatorics acquire parameter-dependent analogues. The presence of the parameter sequence enriches the structure of the ring and allows it to encode information relevant to equivariant geometry and representation theory.

Within these rings, a distinguished basis is introduced. This basis consists of functions that play the role of Schur functions in the classical theory. Just as ordinary Schur functions form a central basis for symmetric functions and have deep connections with tableaux, representation theory, and Schubert calculus, these parameter-dependent analogues serve as the fundamental building blocks in the generalized setting. When two such basis elements are multiplied, the result can again be expanded in the same basis. The coefficients appearing in this expansion are called Littlewood-Richardson polynomials, generalizing the classical Littlewood-Richardson coefficients.

A major part of the work is devoted to giving a combinatorial rule for computing these Littlewood-Richardson polynomials. This rule extends the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule by incorporating the additional parameters into the combinatorics. Importantly, the resulting formula is positive in the sense of W. Graham. That is, the coefficients can be expressed in a form that makes their positivity transparent after rewriting them in appropriate differences of parameters. This positivity is significant because it parallels known positivity phenomena in equivariant Schubert calculus.

The formula is then applied to the study of equivariant Schubert classes on Grassmannians. In this geometric setting, products of Schubert classes are governed by structure coefficients that generalize the usual Schubert calculus constants. The Littlewood-Richardson polynomials arising from the parameter-dependent symmetric functions provide explicit expressions for these coefficients. As a consequence, one obtains a stability property: the structure coefficients for equivariant Schubert classes behave uniformly as the dimensions of the Grassmannians vary. This stability connects finite-dimensional Schubert calculus with the more universal algebra of symmetric functions.

Finally, the text explains another application of the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials to representation theory, specifically to the algebra of Casimir elements for the general linear Lie algebra. Using the theory of quantum immanants, these polynomials describe the multiplication rules among certain central elements. Thus, the same coefficients that control products in the generalized ring of symmetric functions and in equivariant Schubert calculus also govern multiplication in a natural algebra associated with the Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\). This demonstrates the broad significance of the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials across combinatorics, geometry, and representation theory.

A family of parameter-dependent rings of symmetric functions is introduced and studied. These rings extend the classical ring of symmetric functions by incorporating an infinite sequence of parameters, and within them one can define natural analogues of the Schur functions. These generalized Schur functions retain many of the structural features of ordinary Schur functions while encoding additional equivariant or deformation data through the parameters.

A central problem in this setting is to describe the multiplication of these Schur-function analogues. As in the classical theory, the product of two such functions can be expanded in the same basis, with coefficients playing the role of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. In the parameter-dependent theory these coefficients become polynomials, called Littlewood-Richardson polynomials. To compute them, a modified version of Sagan’s combinatorial rule is developed. The rule is formulated in terms of tableaux and provides an explicit positive combinatorial expression for the coefficients.

This formula has an important positivity property: the resulting Littlewood-Richardson polynomials are Graham-positive. In other words, when expressed in the appropriate differences of parameters, their coefficients are nonnegative integers. This positivity is significant because it reflects the expected positivity phenomena in equivariant Schubert calculus.

The theory also has direct geometric consequences. The Littlewood-Richardson polynomials obtained from the modified Sagan-type rule specialize to the stable equivariant Schubert structure coefficients for Grassmannians. Thus the combinatorial rule gives a stable formula for the multiplication of equivariant Schubert classes in the cohomology of Grassmannian varieties.

In addition, the same structure appears in representation theory. The generalized Schur-function basis corresponds to the quantum immanant basis for the center of the universal enveloping algebra of the general linear Lie algebra. Under this correspondence, the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials describe the multiplication of Casimir elements in that basis. Consequently, the combinatorial rule provides not only a tool for equivariant Schubert calculus but also an explicit formula for products of central elements in the representation theory of the general linear Lie algebra.

**The Schur–Littlewood Connection**

The names **Schur** and **Littlewood** are strongly associated with important ideas in algebra, combinatorics, and representation theory. Schur functions, introduced in the work of Issai Schur, are symmetric polynomials that play a central role in the study of partitions, Young tableaux, and representations of the general linear group.

**The** work of Dudley E. Littlewood expanded and developed many of these ideas. Littlewood made major contributions to symmetric functions and representation theory, often using Schur functions as a key tool. Together with related results such as the Littlewood–Richardson rule, these concepts help describe how representations decompose and how symmetric functions multiply.

In modern mathematics, Schur functions and Littlewood’s contributions remain essential. They appear in algebraic geometry, combinatorics, mathematical physics, and the theory of symmetric groups. The connection between Schur and Littlewood shows how abstract algebraic ideas can become powerful tools across many areas of mathematics.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper about factorial Schur functions, Littlewood-Richardson polynomials, equivariant Schubert calculus on Grassmannians, and quantum immanants.
counterfactuals.output: We study the interplay between factorial Schur functions, Littlewood–Richardson polynomials, equivariant Schubert calculus on Grassmannians, and quantum immanants. Factorial Schur functions provide a natural algebraic model for torus-equivariant Schubert classes, while their structure constants are the equivariant Littlewood–Richardson polynomials governing multiplication in the equivariant cohomology of Grassmannians. We develop a unified framework connecting these constants with positivity phenomena, combinatorial tableau formulas, and representation-theoretic constructions arising from quantum immanants. In particular, we describe how factorial analogues of classical symmetric-function identities encode equivariant intersection data and how quantum immanants yield distinguished central elements whose expansions reflect Schubert-theoretic structure. This perspective clarifies the relationship between equivariant Littlewood–Richardson rules and the representation theory of the symmetric and general linear groups, and suggests new pathways for interpreting positivity and stability properties in equivariant and quantum settings. Our results contribute to a broader synthesis of algebraic combinatorics, geometry, and representation theory centered on Grassmannian Schubert calculus.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize in academic style the main results of a paper introducing parameter-dependent rings of symmetric functions and a positive combinatorial rule for their Littlewood-Richardson coefficients.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper develops a parameter-dependent extension of the classical theory of symmetric functions and proves a positive Littlewood–Richardson rule for the corresponding structure constants. Its main contribution is to show that many familiar features of the Schur-function calculus persist in this more general setting, but with coefficients that are polynomial functions of auxiliary parameters.

The authors introduce a ring of symmetric functions depending on a sequence of parameters, often realized through factorial or multiparameter Schur functions. These functions generalize ordinary Schur functions: when the parameters are specialized appropriately, the usual ring of symmetric functions and the classical Schur basis are recovered. The paper establishes that the parameter-dependent Schur functions form a natural basis of the new ring and satisfy analogues of standard properties such as stability, vanishing, and triangularity.

The central result is a positive combinatorial formula for the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients appearing in products of these parameter-dependent Schur functions. In the classical case, the product expansion

\[
s_\lambda s_\mu=\sum_\nu c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}s_\nu
\]

has nonnegative integer coefficients counted by Littlewood–Richardson tableaux. In the parameter-dependent setting, the product has the form

\[
s_\lambda(x\mid a)s_\mu(x\mid a)
=
\sum_\nu c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}(a)\,s_\nu(x\mid a),
\]

where the coefficients \(c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}(a)\) are polynomials in the parameters. The paper gives a tableau rule expressing these coefficients as positive sums of monomials, or products of parameter differences, indexed by suitable decorated or barred tableaux. Thus the formula is cancellation-free and directly generalizes the classical Littlewood–Richardson rule.

A key feature of the result is that it explains the positivity of the generalized coefficients. Rather than defining the coefficients algebraically and proving positivity indirectly, the paper constructs an explicit combinatorial model whose objects are weighted tableaux. Each admissible tableau contributes a positive weight, and the total weight gives the desired coefficient. Under specialization of the parameters to the ordinary symmetric-function case, the extra weights disappear and the rule reduces to the usual Littlewood–Richardson tableau count.

The paper also clarifies structural properties of the generalized coefficients. For example, the coefficients vanish unless the indexing partitions satisfy the expected containment and size conditions, and their degrees reflect the difference between the total degree of the product and the degree of the resulting basis element. These properties parallel geometric phenomena in equivariant Schubert calculus, where factorial Schur functions represent equivariant Schubert classes and the parameter-dependent Littlewood–Richardson coefficients correspond to equivariant structure constants.

Overall, the paper’s main achievement is the construction of a robust parameter-dependent Schur-function theory together with a positive combinatorial multiplication rule. It extends the classical Littlewood–Richardson theory, provides an explicit and computable formula for generalized structure constants, and connects symmetric-function combinatorics with broader themes in representation theory and equivariant geometry.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a mathematical paper abstract explaining how generalized Schur functions yield Littlewood-Richardson polynomials, including applications to equivariant cohomology of Grassmannians and Casimir elements of gl(n).
counterfactuals.output:
We introduce a family of generalized Schur functions whose structure constants provide a polynomial refinement of the classical Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. These Littlewood–Richardson polynomials arise from the expansion of products of generalized Schur functions in the same basis, interpolating between ordinary Schur multiplication and parameter-dependent deformations appearing in equivariant Schubert calculus. We establish determinantal and tableau formulas for these functions, prove positivity properties of the resulting coefficients under natural specializations, and show that the classical Littlewood–Richardson rule is recovered by setting the deformation parameters to zero.

As a first application, we identify these Littlewood–Richardson polynomials with the equivariant structure constants for the cohomology ring \(H_T^*(\operatorname{Gr}(k,n))\) of the Grassmannian. Under this correspondence, generalized Schur functions represent equivariant Schubert classes, and their multiplication encodes the equivariant cup product. This gives a uniform symmetric-function model for equivariant Littlewood–Richardson coefficients and connects tableau combinatorics with localization formulas at torus-fixed points.

As a second application, we relate the same polynomial coefficients to the spectral behavior of higher Casimir elements in the universal enveloping algebra \(U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)\). Via the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, central elements of \(U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)\) act on irreducible polynomial representations by shifted symmetric functions, which appear as specializations of the generalized Schur functions considered here. The resulting Littlewood–Richardson polynomials therefore describe compatibility between tensor product multiplicities, shifted central characters, and Casimir eigenvalues.

These results provide a common framework linking generalized symmetric functions, equivariant Schubert calculus, and the representation theory of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a concise abstract for a paper that modifies Sagan’s Littlewood-Richardson rule to obtain Graham-positive structure constants and relates them to Knutson-Tao puzzles and Okounkov-Olshanski quantum immanants.
counterfactuals.output: We modify Sagan’s Littlewood–Richardson rule to give a positive combinatorial formula for a family of structure constants arising in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. The resulting rule expresses these constants as weighted sums over tableaux and is Graham-positive: each coefficient is a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients in the simple-root variables. We show that the tableaux produced by the modified rule are naturally equivalent to Knutson–Tao puzzles, thereby recovering the puzzle formula from a Littlewood–Richardson perspective. We further identify the same constants with coefficients appearing in the expansion of Okounkov–Olshanski quantum immanants, providing a representation-theoretic interpretation of the combinatorics. These connections unify tableau, puzzle, and quantum-immanant models for equivariant Schubert structure constants and give a new proof of their positivity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a research abstract on double/factorial Schur functions with parameters, manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson polynomial formulas, stability in equivariant Schubert calculus, and multiplication of quantum immanants.
counterfactuals.output: We develop a unified framework for double (factorial) Schur functions with arbitrary parameter sequences, emphasizing positivity phenomena and stability properties arising in equivariant Schubert calculus. Using combinatorial models based on tableaux, factorial divided differences, and stable limits of equivariant Schubert classes, we derive manifestly positive Littlewood–Richardson polynomial formulas for products of double Schur functions. These formulas express structure constants as explicit sums over weighted tableaux or equivalent growth diagrams, with coefficients lying in the positive cone generated by parameter differences, thereby refining classical Littlewood–Richardson coefficients and their equivariant analogues. We prove compatibility of these formulas with stabilization under increasing rank, showing that the corresponding structure constants define stable equivariant Schubert structure constants for Grassmannians and flag varieties. As an application, we relate the resulting factorial Schur expansions to the multiplication of quantum immanants in the enveloping algebra of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\). In particular, we identify positivity-preserving transition coefficients between products of quantum immanants and double Schur bases, revealing a common combinatorial mechanism behind equivariant Schubert multiplication and noncommutative character-like bases. The results provide new positive polynomial rules for factorial Littlewood–Richardson coefficients, clarify their stable behavior, and connect geometric structure constants with representation-theoretic multiplication laws.
